Commission Agenda Report
DATE:  June 10, 2026
TO:  Planning Commission
FROM:  Eric Scherer, Community Development Director
SUBJECT:  CASE NUMBER 45-26CUP - 2080 FOOTHILL BOULEVARD – TO ALLOW THE SALE
  AND ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF BEER AND WINE UNDER THE PRIVILEGES OF A
  TYPE 41 LIQUOR LICENSE AT THE RESTAURANT, LOS JARRITOS, LOCATED AT
  2080 FOOTHILL BOULEVARD

SUMMARY

The applicant, JPLR, Inc. dba Los Jarritos, is requesting approval for a Conditional Use Permit
to obtain an Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Type 41 beer and wine license in conjunction
with their full-service sit-down Mexican restaurant located at 2080 Foothill Boulevard in the La
Verne Plaza shopping center. The restaurant is located within the Foothill Boulevard Specific
Plan zone which requires approval of a conditional use permit for the on-site sale of alcohol.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve Case No. 45-26CUP by adopting
Resolution No. 1358, and affirm a Class 1 exemption (Existing Facilities) from the California
Environmental Quality Act based on this staff report and the findings and conditions of approval
contained in the attached resolution (Attachment 1).

DISCUSSION

BACKGROUND

Los Jarritos is a full-service sit-down Mexican restaurant offering breakfast, lunch and dinner,
coffee and non-alcoholic beverages. The owners/operators of restaurant have 43 years of
experience, most recently operating in two of La Verne’s neighboring cities: Previously in
Pomona on Garey Avenue for 39 years until 2025, and most recently in Claremont on Foothill
Boulevard since the Pomona closure.

Los Jarritos’ new location is at 2080 Foothill Boulevard in the La Verne Plaza shopping center
which is within the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan zone. This location was previously occupied
by The Tenderloin Restaurant for 50 years until 2021 when they moved to 2086 Foothill
Boulevard, a different unit in the same shopping center. They still serve steaks and similar
American cuisine items.

The Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan zone permits the on-site sale of beer, wine, and spirits in
conjunction with an eating establishment when a Conditional Use Permit has been granted. All

  Page 7 of 119
   CASE NO. 45-26CUP - CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT FOR THE SALE AND ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF
  BEER AND WINE (TYPE 41 ALCOHOL LICENSE) FOR LOS JARRITOS RESTAURANT, Page 2

restaurants with on-site sales of beer and wine must comply with California Alcoholic Beverage
Control (ABC) regulations and the sale of alcohol must be incidental to that of food service.

PROPOSAL

The applicant is proposing to add alcohol service in conjunction with their food service under
the privileges of a Type 41 license, which authorizes the holder to sell beer and wine for on-site
consumption. The business must maintain suitable kitchen facilities and must make actual and
substantial sales of meals for consumption on the premises. A Type 41 license also allows
minors to be on the premises.

Minor exterior and interior structural modifications to the tenant space are in the late stages of
being completed with building permits. The restaurant will have an indoor seating capacity of
105 seats and will have 30 employees. As they offer a substantial food/meal menu, the
proposed alcohol service will be incidental and secondary to the primary restaurant use as Los
Jarritos proposes to intend to serve the City as a neighborhood dining establishment focused on
quality food, customers service, and a welcoming atmosphere for families and the surrounding
community. The restaurant will maintain compliance with all applicable state and location
regulations, including requirements of ABC, the LA County Health Department, building and
safety occupancy limitations and public safety standards.

The La Verne Municipal Code limits hours of operation for businesses to between 6:00 a.m. and
12:00 a.m. (midnight). Los Jarritos’ proposed hours of operation are currently 7:00 a.m. – 9:00
p.m. Monday through Sunday, which is compatible with the City’s code. Alcohol Beverage
Control allows alcohol to be served from 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m., which Los Jarritos’ proposed
hours are also compatible with. Staff has included a condition of approval limiting the hours of
the restaurant and alcohol sales to 6:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. (midnight) daily for the restaurant.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES

Los Jarritos will be located in the La Verne Plaza shopping center which is on the south side of
Foothill Boulevard near the intersection of “D” Street and Foothill Boulevard. Within the same
shopping center, there are a variety of land uses including the Tenderloin Restaurant already
mentioned, quick-service food establishments like Little Caesars Pizza and Nothing Bundt
Cakes, banking and tax services, hair and nail salons, as well as dry cleaning, a dental office
and a grocery store. The surrounding land uses include multi-family residential to the south
across Dover Street, and similar commercial uses to the east, west, and north across Foothill
Boulevard.

The City of La Verne Police Department has not expressed any concern with the applicant's
proposed request to operate with this Type 41 license.

A notice of public hearing was published in the Inland Valley Daily Bulletin on May 29th 2026,
and notices were posted at City Hall, on the City’s website and mailed to all property owners
within 300 feet of the subject property on May 28th 2026. Staff has not received any inquiries
about the proposal.

  Page 8 of 119
   CASE NO. 45-26CUP - CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT FOR THE SALE AND ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF
  BEER AND WINE (TYPE 41 ALCOHOL LICENSE) FOR LOS JARRITOS RESTAURANT, Page 3

CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT FINDINGS

Approval of the Conditional Use Permit requires that the Commission make five specific
findings. These findings are set forth in this report’s Attachment 1, Resolution No. 1358, and the
analysis is incorporated by reference.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

This project is categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(a)
(Class 1). The Class 1 exemption is for existing facilities and subsection (a) speaks to the
example of interior or exterior alterations involving such things as tenant improvements. The
proposed project will be located in an existing building and only tenant improvements are
required; there are no exterior improvements proposed as part of the project. The CEQA
exemption is subject to the exceptions of CEQA Guidelines section 15300.2. None of the
exceptions would apply as there are no successive projects of the same type in the same area
that would create a cumulative impact; there are no reasonable possibilities of a significant
impact from the reuse of an existing building; the project will not have any impacts to scenic
highways as it does not involve any new construction; the site is not a hazardous waste site;
and the project does not involve any historical resource.

 Additionally, the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act per Section
15061(b)(3) in that the project/activity is not subject to CEQA due to the activity being covered
by the commonsense exemption, which is that the activity in question will not have any
significant effect on the environment. This commonsense exemption applies because there is
no physical change to the building. No further environmental review is required at this time.

ATTACHMENTS
1.  Attachment 1 - Resolution No. 1358
2.  Attachment 2 - Applicant Narrative
3.  Attachment 3 - Proposed Floor Plan

THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  WHEREAS, on May 11, 2026, JPLR Inc. DBA Los Jarritos Restaurant submitted
an application requesting a Conditional Use Permit to allow the sale and on-site
consumption of beer and wine under the privileges of a Type 41 Liquor License at Los
Jarritos Restaurant located at 2080 Foothill Boulevard; and

  WHEREAS, the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan, and Chapter 18.80 of the La
Verne Municipal Code requires a conditional use permit for this purpose; and

  WHEREAS, Sections 18.108.010 through 18.108.180 of the La Verne Municipal
Code authorizes the Planning Commission to consider such requests subject to certain
findings; and

  WHEREAS, a notice of public hearing was published in the Inland Valley Daily
Bulletin on May 29, 2026 and copies of the notice mailed to all property owners within
300 feet of the subject property on May 28, 2026; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing
on June 10, 2026, taking oral and written testimony;

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Planning Commission of the City
of La Verne:

  Section 1. Environmental Determination. The Planning Commission HEREBY
FINDS and DETERMINES that Case No. 45-26CUP, an application for a Conditional
Use Permit to allow to a conditional use permit for a Type 41 liquor license for the
business, Los Jarritos, is exempt from CEQA based on the following.

This project is categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section
15301(a) (Class 1). The Class 1 exemption is for existing facilities and subsection (a)
speaks to the example of interior or exterior alterations involving such things as tenant
improvements. The proposed project will be located in an existing building and only tenant
improvements are required; there are no exterior improvements proposed as part of the
project. The CEQA exemption is subject to the exceptions of CEQA Guidelines section
15300.2. None of the exceptions would apply as there are no successive projects of the
same type in the same area that would create a cumulative impact; there are no
reasonable possibilities of a significant impact from the reuse of an existing building; the

 project will not have any impacts to scenic highways as it does not involve any new
construction; the site is not a hazardous waste site; and the project does not involve any
historical resource.

Additionally, the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act per
Section 15061(b)(3) in that the project/activity is not subject to CEQA due to the activity
being covered by the common sense exemption, which is that the activity in question
will not have any significant effect on the environment. This commonsense exemption
applies because there is no physical change to the building. No further environmental
review is required at this time. per CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) under the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act, and no further environmental
review is necessary. The exemption is not subject to any of the exceptions set forth in
CEQA Guidelines Section 15

  Section 2. Findings. The Planning Commission HEREBY FINDS and
DETERMINES that the proposed Conditional Use Permit satisfies the findings of
Section 18.108.030 of the La Verne Municipal Code in that:

1.  The proposed use and development are each consistent with the general plan
  and the applicable land use zone.

  Finding: The proposed project is designated Specific Plan Mixed Use by the La
  Verne General Plan and is located within the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan
  Zone. On-site sale of alcoholic beverages is identified as conditionally permitted
  use within the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan, and in conjunction with a bona
  fide restaurant in accordance with Chapter 18.80 of the La Verne Municipal
  Code.

2.  The site for the proposed use is adequate in size, shape, topography,
  accessibility, and other physical characteristics to accommodate the proposed
  use and development in a manner compatible with existing and proposed
  surrounding land uses.

  Finding: The site is a fully developed and is adequate in size, shape, topography
  and accessibility and other physical characteristics to accommodate the
  proposed use in a manner that is compatible with surrounding land uses.

3.  The development site has adequate access to those utilities and other services
  required for the proposed use.

  Finding: The site presently has adequate access to utilities and other services
  that are required for the proposed use.

4.  The proposed use will be arranged, designed, constructed, operated and
  maintained so as to be compatible with the character of the area as intended by
  the general plan.

   Finding: The proposed use is compatible with existing uses within the same
  shopping area, the greater Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan area, and with those
  in the nearby surrounding areas. The use and all associated equipment and

5.  Potential adverse effects upon the surrounding properties will be minimized to

  Finding: It is not expected that there will be any adverse effects on the
  surrounding area. Any potential impacts will be mitigated by conditions of
  approval. The proposed on-site sale of beer and wine serves a public
  convenience or necessity because it will offer an additional choice to La Verne
  residents and increase access to a broader array of products within the City.
  Beer & wine sales are an expected and ordinary activity associated with food
  sales, and that any remaining adverse effects are justified by the benefits

  Section 3. Approval. In accordance with the provisions of the La Verne

  1. Beer and wine sales shall be subject to approval by the Department of Alcoholic

DATE:  June 10, 2026
TO:  Planning Commission
FROM:  Eric Scherer, Community Development Director
SUBJECT:  CASE NO. 56-26DA – FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE GILEAD DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT

SUMMARY
Gilead Sciences, Inc. is requesting approval of a First Amendment to the Development
Agreement originally approved by the City Council on May 5, 2016, under Case No. 79-14DA
for property located within the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan.

The proposed amendment would extend the term of the Development Agreement for an
additional five-year period, retroactively from May 6, 2026 through May 5, 2031, as permitted by
the Agreement. The amendment would also revise Section 7(a) regarding applicable impact
fees during the extended term.

No changes are proposed to the approved land uses, development standards, or project
entitlements. The amendment is intended to maintain continuity of the vested rights and
obligations established under the existing Development Agreement.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission:

  1. Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 1360 recommending that the City Council
  approve the First Amendment to the Development Agreement between the City of La
  Verne and Gilead Sciences, Inc.; and
  2. Determine that the proposed amendment remains within the scope of the previously
  adopted environmental review consisting of the Initial Study/Mitigated Negative
  Declaration and Addendum approved for the project.

DISCUSSION
Development Agreements are authorized under California Government Code Sections 65864
through 65869.5 and allow local governments and property owners to establish a mutually
beneficial framework governing development of property over a specified period of time. In
exchange for public benefits and compliance with agreed-upon conditions, Development
Agreements provide developers with certainty regarding applicable regulations and
development rights.

On May 5, 2016, the City Council approved a Development Agreement with Gilead Sciences,
Inc. under Case No. 79-14DA for a property located within the Arrow Corridor Specific Plan.

  Page 17 of 119
   CASE NO. 56-26DA – FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE GILEAD DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT, Page 2

Section 3 of the Agreement established an initial ten-year term and provided for a one-time five-
year extension by mutual agreement of the parties prior to expiration.

The initial term expired on May 5, 2026. The proposed First Amendment would exercise the
extension provision contained within the Agreement and extend the term for an additional five
years through May 5, 2031. The extension would be applied retroactively to May 6, 2026,
thereby maintaining continuity of the rights, obligations, and protections established under the
Agreement.

The amendment also revises Section 7(a) regarding impact fees. The revised language clarifies
that impact fees applicable during the extended term of the Agreement shall be those in
existence and in effect as of January 1, 2027. This provision establishes certainty regarding fee
obligations during the extension period.

Importantly, the proposed amendment does not modify the approved project, authorize
additional development intensity, change permitted land uses, increase building square footage,
or alter the development standards established under the original Development Agreement. All
provisions of the Development Agreement remain in effect except for the limited amendments
related to term extension and impact fees.

Staff finds that the proposed amendment is consistent with the original intent of the
Development Agreement and supports continued implementation of the approved development

SUBJECT:  ZONING ORDINANCE AMENDMENT – NONCONFORMING LOT
  DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS TO FACILITATE AFFORDABLE HOUSING

SUMMARY
The City of La Verne is proposing an amendment to Section 18.10.060 of the La Verne
Municipal Code, which governs nonconforming uses, lots, and structures. The amendment
would revise the existing provisions related to the merger of contiguous nonconforming lots
under common ownership. Currently, Section 18.10.060(B)(7) requires that adjacent
nonconforming lots under common ownership be merged and treated as a single parcel. While
this provision has historically served to reduce nonconforming development patterns, staff has
identified circumstances where the merger requirement may limit opportunities for the
development of affordable housing.

The proposed ordinance amendment would create a narrowly tailored exception to the lot
merger requirement when application of the merger provision would interfere with the
development of an affordable housing project serving low- or moderate-income households, as
defined by California Health and Safety Code Section 50093. The amendment is intended to
remove a potential regulatory barrier to affordable housing development while maintaining the
City's existing standards for nonconforming lots in all other circumstances.

RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Planning Commission:

  1. Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 1359 recommending that the City Council
  approve an ordinance amending Section 18.10.060 of the La Verne Municipal Code
  related to nonconforming lot development standards to facilitate affordable housing
  opportunities; and
  2. Determine that the proposed ordinance amendment is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3),
  the commonsense exemption.

DISCUSSION
The City is required to continually evaluate and remove governmental constraints that may
hinder the development of housing, particularly affordable housing. During staff's review of the
City's zoning regulations, Section 18.10.060(B)(7) was identified as a potential constraint in
certain situations involving contiguous nonconforming lots held under common ownership.

  Page 112 of 119
   CASE NO. 57-26ZA - ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 18.10.060 OF THE LA VERNE MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  FACILITATE AFFORDABLE HOUSING, Page 2

Under the current code, when two or more nonconforming lots come under common ownership,
they are required to merge into a single parcel. While this requirement can promote orderly
development and reduce nonconforming conditions, it may also prevent the separate
development of individual lots that could otherwise accommodate affordable housing units.
The proposed amendment would provide an exception to the merger requirement when
enforcing the merger would interfere with an affordable housing project for low- or moderate-
income households. The exception would apply only to qualifying affordable housing
developments and would not alter the City's treatment of nonconforming lots in other
circumstances.

The amendment supports State housing policies that encourage local governments to remove
barriers to affordable housing production and is consistent with the goals and policies of the
City's Housing Element. By preserving opportunities to develop housing on individual lots where
affordable housing is proposed, the City can increase flexibility for future affordable housing
projects while maintaining overall zoning consistency.

Because the amendment is limited in scope and applies only to affordable housing
developments meeting specified income qualifications, staff believes the ordinance
appropriately balances housing objectives with the City's long-standing development
regulations.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES
The proposed ordinance amendment is a citywide text amendment and does not involve a
specific development site. As such, no physical development is proposed as part of this action.
The amendment would not alter existing zoning districts, permitted land uses, density
standards, development standards, or land use designations. Instead, it modifies a procedural
provision related to the merger of contiguous nonconforming lots under common ownership.

The amendment does not authorize a specific project or change the types of uses permitted
within any zoning district, therefore it is not anticipated to create land use incompatibilities with
surrounding properties. Any future affordable housing project utilizing the exception would
remain subject to all applicable zoning regulations, development standards, building codes, and
permit requirements. Therefore, staff finds that the proposed ordinance amendment is
compatible with existing and surrounding land uses throughout the City.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
The proposed ordinance amendment is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), commonly referred to as the
"commonsense exemption."

Under Section 15061(b)(3), CEQA applies only to projects that have the potential to cause a
significant effect on the environment. The proposed amendment merely creates an exception to
an existing lot merger requirement when such requirement would interfere with the development
of affordable housing for low- or moderate-income households. The amendment does not
approve any specific development project, authorize new construction, or change allowable
land uses, densities, or development standards.

  Page 113 of 119
   CASE NO. 57-26ZA - ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 18.10.060 OF THE LA VERNE MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  FACILITATE AFFORDABLE HOUSING, Page 3

It can be seen with certainty that the proposed ordinance amendment will not result in a
significant environmental impact, therefore staff finds that the project is exempt from CEQA
pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3).
